claim: Cancer cells exist in a complex ecosystem with numerous other cell types in the tumor microenvironment (TME).
source: Cancer cells exist in a complex ecosystem with numerous other cell types in the tumor microenvironment (TME).
evidence: This is a general statement supported by established scientific knowledge about cancer biology.

claim: The composition of the tumor/TME ecosystem varies at each anatomic site.
source: The composition of this tumor/TME ecosystem will vary at each anatomic site and affects phenotypes such as initiation, metastasis, and drug resistance.
evidence: This statement draws from established understanding of tumor biology and anatomical variation.

claim: The tumor/TME ecosystem affects phenotypes such as initiation, metastasis, and drug resistance.
source: The composition of this tumor/TME ecosystem will vary at each anatomic site and affects phenotypes such as initiation, metastasis, and drug resistance.
evidence: This is supported by established scientific knowledge about how the TME influences cancer behavior.

claim: Zebrafish have a large number of existing cell-type-specific drivers that can label nearly any cell in the TME.
source: Zebrafish are a model system optimized for this problem, because of the large number of existing cell-type-specific drivers that can label nearly any cell in the TME.
evidence: This is supported by the comprehensive database of promoters/enhancers presented in the manuscript and referenced literature.

claim: Cell-type-specific promoters/enhancers in zebrafish can be used to drive fluorophores to facilitate imaging.
source: These cell-type-specific promoters/enhancers can be used to drive fluorophores to facilitate imaging and also CRISPR cassettes to facilitate perturbations.
evidence: This is supported by established zebrafish methodology described throughout the manuscript.

claim: Cell-type-specific promoters/enhancers in zebrafish can be used to drive CRISPR cassettes to facilitate perturbations.
source: These cell-type-specific promoters/enhancers can be used to drive fluorophores to facilitate imaging and also CRISPR cassettes to facilitate perturbations.
evidence: This is supported by CRISPR methodology described in the manuscript and cited literature.

claim: A major advantage of zebrafish is the ease by which large numbers of TME cell types can be studied at once, within the same animal.
source: A major advantage of the zebrafish is the ease by which large numbers of TME cell types can be studied at once, within the same animal.
evidence: This is inferred from the capabilities of zebrafish described throughout the manuscript.

claim: Cancers resemble ecosystems composed of both tumor and microenvironmental components.
source: Cancers are recognized to resemble ecosystems composed of both tumor and microenvironmental components (Joyce and Pollard, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Joyce and Pollard, 2009.

claim: The tumor microenvironment is especially important for clinically relevant endpoints such as drug resistance and metastasis.
source: The tumor microenvironment (TME) is especially important for clinically relevant endpoints such as drug resistance and metastasis, the major causes of cancer mortality.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge about cancer biology and clinical outcomes.

claim: Drug resistance and metastasis are the major causes of cancer mortality.
source: The tumor microenvironment (TME) is especially important for clinically relevant endpoints such as drug resistance and metastasis, the major causes of cancer mortality.
evidence: This is supported by established clinical knowledge about cancer outcomes.

claim: The TME is composed of a highly heterogeneous collection of cells, proteins, and soluble factors that can all affect tumor phenotypes.
source: The TME itself is composed of a highly heterogeneous collection of cells, proteins, and soluble factors that can all affect tumor phenotypes.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge about TME composition.

claim: There is long-range communication between the tumor and distant parts of the body through secreted factors such as hormones, cytokines, and extracellular vesicles.
source: Adding to this complexity is the long-range communication between the tumor and distant parts of the body through secreted factors such as hormones, cytokines, and extracellular vesicles (Peinado et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Peinado et al., 2017.

claim: The mouse remains the mainstay for TME studies.
source: The mouse remains the mainstay for such studies, given the wide range of genetic tools, tumor models, and established protocols.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge about cancer research models.

claim: Major strengths of mouse models include close homology to human disease and the ability to express transgenes in both an inducible and tissue-specific manner.
source: The major strengths of mouse models include the close homology to human disease and the ability to express transgenes in both an inducible and tissue-specific manner (Hill et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hill et al., 2021 and established knowledge about mouse models.

claim: The mouse remains a challenging model to perturb the TME at large scale.
source: Despite its strengths, the mouse remains a challenging model to perturb the TME at large scale, since it often requires breeding of multiple alleles to study one or two genes in specific TME cell types.
evidence: This is inferred from the practical limitations of mouse breeding described in the text.

claim: High-resolution in vivo imaging in the mouse remains highly specialized and is difficult to achieve at the single cell level.
source: Additionally, high-resolution in vivo imaging in the mouse remains highly specialized (Patsialou et al., 2013) and is difficult to achieve at the single cell level.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Patsialou et al., 2013 and inference about technical limitations.

claim: Organoid models can model both intratumor heterogeneity as well as interactions with specific cell types in the TME.
source: Organoid models have received increased attention due to their ability to model both intratumor heterogeneity as well as interactions with specific cell types in the TME (Neal et al., 2018) but are largely limited to studying one or two TME cell types.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Neal et al., 2018.

claim: Organoid models are largely limited to studying one or two TME cell types.
source: Organoid models have received increased attention due to their ability to model both intratumor heterogeneity as well as interactions with specific cell types in the TME (Neal et al., 2018) but are largely limited to studying one or two TME cell types.
evidence: This is inferred from the limitations of organoid technology.

claim: Zebrafish share 70% of their genome with humans.
source: Zebrafish are small (2–5 cm) tropical fish that share 70% of their genome with humans, and more than 80% of disease-associated genes are conserved (Patton et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Patton et al., 2021.

claim: More than 80% of disease-associated genes are conserved between zebrafish and humans.
source: Zebrafish are small (2–5 cm) tropical fish that share 70% of their genome with humans, and more than 80% of disease-associated genes are conserved (Patton et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Patton et al., 2021.

claim: Zebrafish are easy to genetically manipulate at large scale.
source: Its major strengths are that it is easy to genetically manipulate at large scale and is highly optimized for in vivo imaging.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge about zebrafish methodology described throughout the manuscript.

claim: Zebrafish are highly optimized for in vivo imaging.
source: Its major strengths are that it is easy to genetically manipulate at large scale and is highly optimized for in vivo imaging.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge about zebrafish imaging capabilities described throughout the manuscript.

claim: Zebrafish are amenable to chemical screens, allowing for identification of bioactive small molecules.
source: It is also amenable to chemical screens, allowing for identification of bioactive small molecules.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge about zebrafish screening capabilities.

claim: The rag2 promoter was used to drive the MYC oncogene, resulting in T-cell leukemia in zebrafish.
source: The first clear example of this was a transgenic animal in which the T-cell-specific rag2 promoter was used to drive the MYC oncogene (Langenau et al., 2003), which resulted in T-cell leukemia in the animals.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Langenau et al., 2003.

claim: The melanocyte-specific mitfa promoter was used to drive BRAFV600E, and those animals developed melanoma that closely resemble the patient disease.
source: Along the same lines, the melanocyte-specific mitfa promoter was used to drive BRAFV600E (the most frequently mutated gene in human melanoma) and those animals developed melanoma that closely resemble the patient disease (Patton et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Patton et al., 2005.

claim: BRAFV600E is the most frequently mutated gene in human melanoma.
source: Along the same lines, the melanocyte-specific mitfa promoter was used to drive BRAFV600E (the most frequently mutated gene in human melanoma) and those animals developed melanoma that closely resemble the patient disease (Patton et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge about melanoma genetics.

claim: The mitfa promoter has been used to drive expression of novel melanoma oncogenes such as SETDB1, SOX10, and GDF6 in melanocytes.
source: This same mitfa promoter fragment has been widely utilized in modifier screens on top of BRAFV600E to drive expression of novel melanoma oncogenes such as SETDB1 (Ceol et al., 2011), SOX10 (Kaufman et al., 2016), and GDF6 (Venkatesan et al., 2018) in melanocytes.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ceol et al., 2011, Kaufman et al., 2016, and Venkatesan et al., 2018.

claim: The mitfa promoter has been used to drive Cas9 to inactivate SPRED1 specifically in melanocytes.
source: This mitfa promoter has been used to drive Cas9 to inactivate genes specifically in melanocytes, such as SPRED1, an important tumor suppressor in mucosal melanoma (Ablain et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ablain et al., 2018.

claim: SPRED1 is an important tumor suppressor in mucosal melanoma.
source: This mitfa promoter has been used to drive Cas9 to inactivate genes specifically in melanocytes, such as SPRED1, an important tumor suppressor in mucosal melanoma (Ablain et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ablain et al., 2018.

claim: Zebrafish can be used for tumor cell transplantation at both larval/embryonic stages and adult stages.
source: In addition to transgenic models, the zebrafish has also extensively been used as a model for tumor cell transplantation. This can be done at both larval/embryonic stages (prior to the development of adaptive immunity) as well as adult stages (which need to be immuncompromised due to immune rejection).
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge about zebrafish transplantation methods.

claim: Larval/embryonic zebrafish transplantation is done prior to the development of adaptive immunity.
source: This can be done at both larval/embryonic stages (prior to the development of adaptive immunity) as well as adult stages (which need to be immuncompromised due to immune rejection).
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge about zebrafish immune development.

claim: Adult zebrafish need to be immunocompromised for transplantation due to immune rejection.
source: This can be done at both larval/embryonic stages (prior to the development of adaptive immunity) as well as adult stages (which need to be immuncompromised due to immune rejection).
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge about immune rejection in transplantation.

claim: Zebrafish transplantation can be done using either zebrafish-derived or human-derived cell lines.
source: This can be done using either zebrafish-derived (Heilmann et al., 2015) or human-derived cell lines (Yan et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Heilmann et al., 2015 and Yan et al., 2019.

claim: Most components of the TME are conserved between zebrafish and humans.
source: Most components of the TME are conserved between zebrafish and humans, although there are important exceptions which we discuss below.
evidence: This is inferred from comparative biology and the discussion of specific cell types throughout the manuscript.

claim: The ease of high-quality imaging in zebrafish stems from its small size and optical transparency.
source: The ease of high-quality imaging stems from its small size (4 mm–12 mm in embryos/larvae and ~2–5 cm in adults) and optical transparency (Singleman and Holtzman, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Singleman and Holtzman, 2014 and established knowledge about zebrafish imaging.

claim: An entire zebrafish embryo/larvae can be placed on a confocal and multi-photon microscope.
source: The smaller size makes it possible for an entire zebrafish embryo/larvae to be placed on a confocal and multi-photon microscope.
evidence: This is inferred from the physical dimensions of zebrafish and microscopy capabilities.

claim: The ability to image an entire animal at single-cell resolution enables investigation of not just local microenvironmental interactions but also distant 'whole body' interactions.
source: The ability to image an entire animal at single-cell resolution enables investigation of not just local microenvironmental interactions but also distant 'whole body' interactions (Loveless et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Loveless et al., 2020.

claim: Metastasis is classically separated into at least four steps: intravasation from the primary site, circulation in blood stream, extravasation at distant sites, and outgrowth at those sites.
source: This is particularly important for understanding the contribution of the TME to metastasis, which is classically separated into at least four steps: intravasation from the primary site, circulation in blood stream, extravasation at distant sites, and outgrowth at those sites (Gupta and Massagué, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Gupta and Massagué, 2006.

claim: Zebrafish can be used to image and quantify each step of metastasis in a single animal.
source: In contrast, the zebrafish can be used to image and quantify each of these steps in a single animal, since it is highly amenable to standard epifluorescence microscopy (for many cells), confocal microscopy (for single cells), and lightsheet microscopy (even now including whole embryo and adult animals).
evidence: This is inferred from the imaging capabilities of zebrafish described in the manuscript.

claim: Spatial transcriptomics is a new RNA-sequencing technology that provides spatial resolution to gene expression.
source: Spatial transcriptomics is a new RNA-sequencing technology that provides spatial resolution to gene expression and has already provided key insights into cancer-TME interactions (Longo et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Longo et al., 2021.

claim: An entire adult zebrafish section can fit on a slide used for spatial transcriptomics.
source: In contrast to mouse models, an entire adult zebrafish section can fit on a slide used for spatial transcriptomics thereby enabling investigation not just of local interactions but whole-body interactions.
evidence: This is inferred from the size comparison between zebrafish and mice.

claim: Spatial transcriptomics paired with single-cell RNA-sequencing identified a distinct 'interface' cell state in both tumor and TME cells in a BRAFV600E model of melanoma.
source: In a BRAFV600E model of melanoma, spatial transcriptomics paired with single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) identified a distinct 'interface' cell state in both tumor and TME cells where they are in physical contact with one another.
evidence: This is supported by data from Hunter et al., 2021 as referenced in the text.

claim: The 'interface' cell state is associated with upregulation of cilia genes.
source: This cell state is associated with upregulation of cilia genes, and its function is an area of investigation (Hunter et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hunter et al., 2021.

claim: The smaller size of zebrafish makes it feasible to work with hundreds or thousands of animals for an experiment.
source: In addition to spatial transcriptomics, the smaller size of the zebrafish makes it feasible to work with hundreds or thousands of animals for an experiment and increases the statistical rigor in a way that is not feasible in mice.
evidence: This is inferred from the practical advantages of zebrafish size and housing.

claim: Zebrafish embryos can be placed in a 96-well plate for chemical screening.
source: Zebrafish embryos can be placed in a 96-well plate for chemical screening (Patton et al., 2021), and 1 liter of space can house many more fish than mice.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Patton et al., 2021.

claim: A single zebrafish breeding pair can yield hundreds of embryos.
source: A single breeding pair can yield hundreds of embryos in contrast to approximately a dozen offspring in mice.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge about zebrafish breeding.

claim: A single mouse breeding pair yields approximately a dozen offspring.
source: A single breeding pair can yield hundreds of embryos in contrast to approximately a dozen offspring in mice.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge about mouse breeding.

claim: Most zebrafish imaging has traditionally been done during the embryonic and larval stages.
source: Most zebrafish imaging has traditionally been done during the embryonic and larval stages, since those young animals are naturally transparent.
evidence: This is supported by established practice in zebrafish research.

claim: In the larval xenograft assay, fluorescently labeled cancer cells are transplanted into the circulation of the developing animal.
source: In the larval xenograft assay, fluorescently labeled cancer cells are transplanted into the circulation of the developing animal.
evidence: This is a description of an established methodology.

claim: The human RhoC gene engineered into human cancer cell lines and transplanted into fli1a-GFP transgenics revealed that these cells 'open up' the vasculature via secretion of VEGF.
source: For example, the human RhoC gene was engineered into a variety of human cancer cell lines and then transplanted into fli1a-GFP (green fluorescent protein) transgenics, which revealed that these cells 'open up' the vasculature via secretion of VEGF, which ultimately allows them to invade into new tissues (Hoeppner et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hoeppner et al., 2015.

claim: The larval xenograft assay can be used to study metastasis and drug response, such as the anti-VEGF molecule bevacizumab using PDX models.
source: This larval xenograft assay can also be used to study metastasis and drug response, such as the anti-VEGF molecule bevacizumab using PDX (patient-derived xenograft) models (Rebelo de Almeida et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Rebelo de Almeida et al., 2020.

claim: A xenograft of melanoma cells co-cultured with lymphatic endothelial cells revealed an increase in distant cancer cell dissemination in zebrafish.
source: A xenograft of melanoma cells co-cultured with lymphatic endothelial cells revealed an increase in distant cancer cell dissemination in zebrafish (Pekkonen et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Pekkonen et al., 2018.

claim: Macrophages have been shown to be required for tumor angiogenesis by coupling the larval xenograft assay with cell ablation approaches.
source: By coupling this assay with cell ablation approaches, the role of certain cell types such as macrophages has been shown to be required for tumor angiogenesis, a key component of tumor growth (Britto et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Britto et al., 2018.

claim: The larval xenograft model has been extended into patient 'avatars' to investigate responses to specific drugs in vivo.
source: This model has recently been extended into patient 'avatars' to investigate responses to specific drugs in vivo (Fazio et al., 2020; Fior et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Fazio et al., 2020 and Fior et al., 2017.

claim: Cancer cells from the same patient generate different TMEs through differential recruitment of neutrophils and macrophages, resulting in opposing implantation kinetics.
source: Using two matched patient-derived colorectal cancer cell lines from the primary tumor as well as a lymph node metastasis in a larval xenograft assay, a recent study revealed how cancer cells from the same patient generate different TMEs through differential recruitment of neutrophils and macrophages, resulting in opposing implantation kinetics.
evidence: This is supported by data from Póvoa et al., 2021 as referenced in the text.

claim: scRNA-seq indicated IFN/Notch vs IL10 signaling in mediating subclonal selection of escaper cells in colorectal cancer.
source: Subsequent scRNA-seq indicated IFN/Notch vs IL10 signaling in mediating subclonal selection of escaper cells, pointing to a role for innate immunity (Póvoa et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Póvoa et al., 2021.

claim: The larval xenograft assay is very rapid and can usually be readout in 1–5 days post-transplant.
source: The assay is very rapid, can usually be readout in 1–5 days post-transplant, and is easily amenable to single-cell imaging.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge about the larval xenograft assay timeline.

claim: Important discoveries from transgenic cancer models at early developmental timepoints include the tumorigenic consequences of the wound-associated recruitment of neutrophils.
source: Important discoveries from these models include the tumorigenic consequences of the wound-associated recruitment of neutrophils, the ability of innate immune cells to promote tumor invasion through proteolytic breaching of the basement membrane, and the pro-tumoral effects of leukocyte-derived PGE2 (Antonio et al., 2015; Feng et al., 2012; Feng et al., 2010; van den Berg et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Antonio et al., 2015; Feng et al., 2012; Feng et al., 2010; van den Berg et al., 2019.

claim: Innate immune cells can promote tumor invasion through proteolytic breaching of the basement membrane.
source: Important discoveries from these models include the tumorigenic consequences of the wound-associated recruitment of neutrophils, the ability of innate immune cells to promote tumor invasion through proteolytic breaching of the basement membrane, and the pro-tumoral effects of leukocyte-derived PGE2 (Antonio et al., 2015; Feng et al., 2012; Feng et al., 2010; van den Berg et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Antonio et al., 2015; Feng et al., 2012; Feng et al., 2010; van den Berg et al., 2019.

claim: Leukocyte-derived PGE2 has pro-tumoral effects.
source: Important discoveries from these models include the tumorigenic consequences of the wound-associated recruitment of neutrophils, the ability of innate immune cells to promote tumor invasion through proteolytic breaching of the basement membrane, and the pro-tumoral effects of leukocyte-derived PGE2 (Antonio et al., 2015; Feng et al., 2012; Feng et al., 2010; van den Berg et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Antonio et al., 2015; Feng et al., 2012; Feng et al., 2010; van den Berg et al., 2019.

claim: Adaptive immunity (i.e. T and B cells) as well as stromal cells are not present in embryos and arise later in adulthood.
source: In particular, adaptive immunity (i.e. T and B cells) as well as stromal cells are key components of the TME that are not present in embryos and arise later in adulthood (Minchin and Rawls, 2017; Page et al., 2013; Trede et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Minchin and Rawls, 2017; Page et al., 2013; Trede et al., 2004.

claim: The casper strain of zebrafish is more optically transparent and amenable to adult imaging.
source: Recognizing that these studies would be enhanced if they could be done in adult animals, we previously developed a more optically transparent strain of zebrafish called casper that is amenable to adult imaging (White et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to White et al., 2008.

claim: Casper fish were used for allograft experiments to identify a requirement for endothelin (EDN3) signaling from the TME in melanoma cell dissemination.
source: We initially used this line for allograft experiments, in which the donor tumor cells were derived from a transgenic zebrafish (i.e. ZMEL1-GFP cells), which allowed us to identify a requirement for endothelin (EDN3) signaling from the TME in melanoma cell dissemination (Kim et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kim et al., 2017.

claim: Adult immunocompromised casper fish have been generated for xenograft studies using human cancer cell lines or PDXs.
source: Toward that end, adult immunocompromised casper fish have now been generated, such that xenograft studies using human cancer cell lines or PDXs can also be performed (Yan et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Yan et al., 2019.

claim: Adult immunocompromised casper fish have been used for drug studies, revealing the efficacy of PARP inhibitors and DNA-damaging agents in rhabdomyosarcoma.
source: This has been used for drug studies, revealing the efficacy of PARP inhibitors and DNA-damaging agents in rhabdomyosarcoma, and responses to immune therapies as well.
evidence: This is inferred from the drug studies mentioned in the context of Yan et al., 2019.

claim: The combination of small size and optical transparency enables continuous live imaging in zebrafish.
source: The combination of small size and optical transparency also enables continuous live imaging.
evidence: This is inferred from the physical properties of zebrafish and imaging capabilities.

claim: In mice, high-resolution live imaging typically requires sacrificing the animal or utilizing highly specialized techniques that are often invasive.
source: In mice, high-resolution live imaging typically requires sacrificing the animal or utilizing highly specialized techniques that are often invasive (Stoletov et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Stoletov et al., 2007.

claim: Zebrafish embryos/larvae are ideal for imaging cell-cell interactions for hours or even days.
source: In contrast, zebrafish embryos/larvae in particular are ideal for imaging cell-cell interactions for hours or even days.
evidence: This is inferred from the imaging capabilities of zebrafish described in the manuscript.

claim: Continuous confocal imaging demonstrated extravasation of circulating tumor cell clusters with invasive cells on the leading edge and proliferative cells following.
source: By isolating cell lines enriched for one state vs another and transplanting them into embryos, continuous confocal imaging demonstrated extravasation of circulating tumor cell clusters with invasive cells on the leading edge and proliferative cells following.
evidence: This is supported by data from Campbell et al., 2021 as referenced in the text.

claim: The transcription factor TFAP2 is the major regulator of divergent cell states in melanoma metastasis.
source: Continuous high-resolution imaging in combination with facile transgenesis was essential to identify the transcription factor TFAP2 as the major regulator of these divergent cell states (Campbell et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Campbell et al., 2021.

claim: Live imaging of xenografts in zebrafish embryos found that low flow vessels favor tumor cell arrest, but high flow favors endothelial remodeling that permits efficient extravasation.
source: Similarly, live imaging of xenografts in zebrafish embryos was used to investigate the role of hemodynamic flow forces in the arrest, adhesion, and extravasation of circulating tumor cells finding that low flow vessels favor tumor cell arrest, but high flow favors endothelial remodeling that permits efficient extravasation (Follain et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Follain et al., 2018.

claim: In melanoma, tumors largely arise in melanocyte precursors, which are surrounded by keratinocytes, fibroblasts, and adipocytes.
source: For example, in melanoma, the tumors largely arise in melanocyte precursors, which are surrounded by the normal resident cells of the skin – keratinocytes, fibroblasts, and adipocytes (Golan et al., 2015; Kaur et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Golan et al., 2015; Kaur et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2018.

claim: Normal resident cells of the skin play roles in shaping tumor phenotypes such as proliferation and invasion.
source: These seemingly normal resident cells all play roles in shaping tumor phenotypes such as proliferation and invasion.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge about TME interactions.

claim: The crosstalk between TME cells and tumor cells is likely to be bidirectional.
source: The crosstalk between TME cells and tumor cells is likely to be bidirectional, in that each cell will undergo changes when next to each other.
evidence: This is inferred from the understanding of cell-cell interactions in cancer biology.

claim: Normal fibroblasts take on new transcriptional characteristics to become 'cancer-associated fibroblasts'.
source: For example, it is now well understood that normal fibroblasts take on new transcriptional characteristics to become 'cancer-associated fibroblasts' (Sahai et al., 2020); similarly, 'tumor-associated macrophages' can be altered in the presence of a tumor to take on either pro or anti-tumorigenic properties (Quail and Joyce, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Sahai et al., 2020.

claim: Tumor-associated macrophages can be altered in the presence of a tumor to take on either pro or anti-tumorigenic properties.
source: For example, it is now well understood that normal fibroblasts take on new transcriptional characteristics to become 'cancer-associated fibroblasts' (Sahai et al., 2020); similarly, 'tumor-associated macrophages' can be altered in the presence of a tumor to take on either pro or anti-tumorigenic properties (Quail and Joyce, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Quail and Joyce, 2017.

claim: Soluble factors like TGF-beta from stromal cells can enact broad transcriptional rewiring of recipient tumor cells.
source: Soluble factors like TGF-beta from stromal cells can enact broad transcriptional rewiring of recipient tumor cells, but there are likely other metabolic or cell-cell mechanisms that epigenetically rewire the tumor cell as well.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge about TGF-beta signaling in cancer.

claim: LIF enacts epigenetic changes to convert fibroblasts into CAFs.
source: For example, LIF is known to enact epigenetic changes to convert fibroblasts into CAFs (cancer-associated fibroblasts) (Albrengues et al., 2015), and pancreatic stellate cells can be reprogrammed by Vitamin D (Sherman et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Albrengues et al., 2015.

claim: Pancreatic stellate cells can be reprogrammed by Vitamin D.
source: For example, LIF is known to enact epigenetic changes to convert fibroblasts into CAFs (cancer-associated fibroblasts) (Albrengues et al., 2015), and pancreatic stellate cells can be reprogrammed by Vitamin D (Sherman et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Sherman et al., 2014.

claim: Most cell-type-specific promoters/enhancers in zebrafish were originally studied in the context of developmental biology.
source: The majority of these cell-type-specific promoter/enhancers were originally studied in the context of developmental biology.
evidence: This is supported by the historical context of zebrafish research described in the manuscript.

claim: A promoter fragment of the mitfa gene was used to drive GFP, allowing for visualization of when and where melanocytes are specified during embryogenesis.
source: For example, as mentioned above, a promoter fragment of the mitfa gene, which is specific to melanocytes, was used to drive GFP, allowing for visualization of when and where melanocytes are specified during embryogenesis (Lister et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lister et al., 1999.

claim: krt4 is a promoter for superficial keratinocytes.
source: Many other skin promoters have been identified: krt4 for superficial keratinocytes (Ju et al., 1999), tp63 for basal keratinocytes (Eisenhoffer et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2014), and plin2 for adipocytes (Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ju et al., 1999.

claim: tp63 is a promoter for basal keratinocytes.
source: Many other skin promoters have been identified: krt4 for superficial keratinocytes (Ju et al., 1999), tp63 for basal keratinocytes (Eisenhoffer et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2014), and plin2 for adipocytes (Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Eisenhoffer et al., 2017 and Lee et al., 2014.

claim: plin2 is a promoter for adipocytes.
source: Many other skin promoters have been identified: krt4 for superficial keratinocytes (Ju et al., 1999), tp63 for basal keratinocytes (Eisenhoffer et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2014), and plin2 for adipocytes (Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2018.

claim: cd79 is a promoter for B-cells.
source: The blood system has many promoters that allow for imaging and isolation of specific cell types: cd79 for B-cells (Liu et al., 2017), lck/rag2 for T-cells (Jessen et al., 2001; Langenau et al., 2004; Langenau and Zon, 2005), and mpeg1 for macrophages (Ellett et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Liu et al., 2017.

claim: lck/rag2 are promoters for T-cells.
source: The blood system has many promoters that allow for imaging and isolation of specific cell types: cd79 for B-cells (Liu et al., 2017), lck/rag2 for T-cells (Jessen et al., 2001; Langenau et al., 2004; Langenau and Zon, 2005), and mpeg1 for macrophages (Ellett et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jessen et al., 2001; Langenau et al., 2004; Langenau and Zon, 2005.

claim: mpeg1 is a promoter for macrophages.
source: The blood system has many promoters that allow for imaging and isolation of specific cell types: cd79 for B-cells (Liu et al., 2017), lck/rag2 for T-cells (Jessen et al., 2001; Langenau et al., 2004; Langenau and Zon, 2005), and mpeg1 for macrophages (Ellett et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ellett et al., 2011.

claim: fli1a marks endothelial cells lining blood vessels.
source: A broadly useful promoter has been fli1a, which marks the endothelial cells lining blood vessels and has been widely used in many developmental and regenerative studies due to its high specificity and strong expression (Lawson and Weinstein, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lawson and Weinstein, 2002.

claim: The DANIO-CODE consortium has comprehensively cataloged ~140,000 cis-regulatory regions in zebrafish development.
source: Beyond the known promoter/enhancer regions cloned by the zebrafish community, a recent exciting advance comes from the international DANIO-CODE consortium (Baranasic et al., 2022), which has comprehensively cataloged ~140,000 cis-regulatory regions in zebrafish development, many of which will mark specific cell types and states.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Baranasic et al., 2022.

claim: A random insertional screen identified a neuronal subpopulation of cells essential for fear conditioning.
source: For example, a recent study using this approach identified a neuronal subpopulation of cells essential for fear conditioning (Lal et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lal et al., 2018.

claim: Zebrafish have gills instead of lungs.
